AGAINST THE IMPUGNED ORDER DATED 09.06.2023 PASSED BY LD. MM-02, MAHILA COURT, NORTH DISTRICT, ROHINI COURTS, DELHI IN CASE TITLED AS 'STATE VS. PRAMOD KUMAR @ SONU & ORS.'

U/S 498A/406/34 IPC PS MANGOLPURI 1

. Vide this order, I shall decide the revision petition being filed by the revisionists/accused against the impugned order dated 09.06.2023 titled as 'State Vs. Pramod Kumar @ Sonu' in case FIR No.107/2010 u/s 498A/406/34 IPC PS Mangolpuri passed by ld. MM-02, Mahila Court, North District, Rohini Courts, Delhi whereby the application u/s 300 Cr.P.C. being filed by the revisionist/accused has been dismissed by the court of ld. MM.
2.

sentences.text: That, the brief material facts to decide this revision petition are that complainant in the aforesaid case FIR was married with the revisionist/accused no.1 on 02.03.2006 and immediately after the marriage, the in-laws of the complainant started to give beatings and harassed her for demand of dowry.
The complainant had given birth to a baby boy on dated 18.11.2006 but the revisionist/accused no.1/husband of complainant did not turn up to lookafter his newly born baby.

A typed complaint was made by the complainant addressed to the ACP, Crime Against Women Cell,
Pitampura, Delhi alleging that she has been harassed for demand of dowry and on her complaint, an FIR bearing no.107/2010 u/s 498A/406/34 IPC PS Mangolpuri was registered.

After investigation of the said case FIR, the IO has filed the charge-sheet in the court of ld. MM but simultaneously, the Pramod Kumar vs State on 18 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/2565142/
1 complainant has also filed another similar complaint on the same allegations dated 11.05.2011 before Police Station Manjhola, District Muradabad, U.P. and on the same facts and allegations,
another FIR bearing no.326/11 Case Crime No.883/11 u/s 323/504/498A IPC and Section 3/4 of Dowry Prohibition Act was registered against the revisionist herein.

sentences.text:
3. Ld. counsel for the revisionist has submitted that the trial of the case FIR No.326/2011 was concluded and the ld. Court of ACJM, Court no.2, Muradabad, U.P. vide order dated 25.03.2016 had passed the judgement and acquitted all the revisionists/accused and if the complete trial has been concluded and the revisionist/accused have been acquitted in the said case FIR registered in District Muradabad, U.P. on the same facts and allegations, then, as per the provisions of Section 300 Cr.P.C., the proceedings of the case FIR No.107/2010 u/s 498A/406/34 IPC PS Mangolpuri ought to have been dropped but his application u/s 300 Cr.P.C. was dismissed by the court of ld. MM vide impugned order dated 09.06.2023.
4.
It has also been submitted that it is a matter of double jeopardy as the ingredients of Section 406 IPC are resemble with the ingredient of Section 3/4 of Dowry Prohibition Act but the ld.
Trial court has not considered these facts and was pleased to dismiss the application u/s 300 Cr.P.C. without application of judicial mind and the ld.
Trial court has also ignored the judgement passed by the ld.

Trial court of District Muradabad (U.P.) in case FIR No.326/2011 Crime Case No.883/11 u/s 323/504/498A IPC and Section 3/4 of Dowry Prohibition Act whereby all the revisionists/accused have been acquitted.
5. By way of the present revision petition, it is prayed that the impugned order dated 09.06.2023 passed by the ld.

Trial court in case FIR No.107/2010 u/s 498A/406/34 IPC PS Mangolpuri may kindly be rectified in view of the provisions of Section 300 of Cr.P.C. and all the revisionists/accused may kindly be discharged.

6. That, upon notice of the revision petition to the State, the ld.
APP for the State has not filed any reply of the instant revision petition and has argued straightaway.
It is submitted by ld. APP for the State that there is no illegality or irregularity in the impugned order dated 09.06.2023 passed by the ld.
Trial court and the revision petition has been filed only to waste the precious time of this court and the same may kindly be dismissed.

7. Having heard the submissions made by ld. counsel for all the revisionists as well as ld. APP for the State and after gone through the averments of the revision petition and also after gone through the trial court record as well as the impugned order dated 09.06.2023 passed by the ld. MM-02, Mahila Courts, North District, Rohini Courts, Delhi, this court is of the considered view that Section 300(1)
Cr.P.C. provides as follows:-
"300. Person once convicted or acquitted not be tried for same offence.

entities.text: Mahila Courts, North District, Rohini Courts, Delhi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
(1) A person who has once been tried by a Court of competent jurisdiction for an offence and convicted or acquitted of such offence shall, while such conviction or Pramod Kumar vs State on 18 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/2565142/
2 acquittal remains in force, not be liable to be tried again for the same offence, nor on the same facts for any other offence for which a different charge from the one made against him might have been made under sub- section (1) of section 221, or for which he might have been convicted under sub- section (2) thereof."

sentences.text:
8. Perusal of the ingredients of Section 300 Cr.P.C., the intention of the Legislature was quite clear on the point that if an accused has been tried by a court of competent jurisdiction for an offence and the judgment is pronounced whether the accused are convicted or acquitted, then, on the same facts,
the subsequent trial cannot be done.

9. It is worth mentioning that the revisionist/accused has faced the trial in case FIR NO.326/2011 u/s 498A/323/504 IPC and 3/4 Dowry Prohibition Act and in that trial, the testimony of the complainant namely Meenakshi was recorded.

The testimony of the mother of the complainant Smt.
Draupadi was also recorded and in their testimony, neither the complainant nor her mother has alleged that the revisionist/accused had ever harassed the complainant for demand of dowry.

After concluding the trial, the ld. Court/Chief Judicial Magistrate No.2, Muradabad (U.P.) vide order dated 25.03.2014 acquitted all the revisionist/ accused for the offence u/s 498A/323/504 IPC and Section 3/4 of Dowry Prohibition Act.
The view taken by the ld.

Trial court that the trial of the offence u/s 498A IPC has only been carried out by the court of Chief Judicial Magistrate,
Muradabad, U.P. and therefore, the revisionist/accused are acquitted and there is a offence u/s 406 IPC in FIR No. 107/2010 in case titled as 'State Vs. Pramod @ Sonu' PS Mangolpuri and they have to face the trial

entities.text: State Vs. Pramod @ Sonu' PS Mangolpuri
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: . This view of ld. Trial court is not sustainable in the eyes of law and it appears that the ld. Trial court has oversighted the provisions of double jeopardy i.e. Section 300 of Cr.P.C. inasmuch as the facts as well as averments of complaint are the same and allegations are also the same in both the FIR No.326/11 PS Manjhaula, District Muradabad, U.P. and in the FIR no.107/2010 PS Mangolpuri, Delhi and once the acquittal order has been passed in case FIR No.326/11 PS Manjhaula, District Muradabad, U.P. on the same facts and allegations, then, the subsequent trial in case FIR No.107/2010 PS Mangolpuri is not justified in any manner.
Therefore, considering all the facts and circumstances, this court is of the considered view that the impugned order dated 09.06.2023 passed by the ld.
Trial court, MM-02, Mahila Court, North- District, Rohini Court, Delhi is not sustainable.

entities.text: Mahila Court, North- District, Rohini Court, Delhi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Hence, the same is set aside.
The proceedings against all the revisionists/ accused in case FIR No.107/2010 in case State Vs. Pramod @ Sonu & Ors.
is hereby dropped.
The revision petition stands allowed and disposed off accordingly.
10. TCR, if any, be sent back to the ld.
Trial court with copy of this order.
11. File be consigned to record room.
